feedback: Written before this candidate races. Race 2 (score 356.98, entityR2B) showed that 16 mm footprints fixed oval (15/20 finishes, max_error 0.048) but not s-bend or slalom, which still end 40/40 off_track with line_loss about 1.1 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. That pattern means the outer sensors are still not reaching the line during drift. Race 1 (entityR2A, 302.7) showed that widening from ±0.02 to ±0.03 m improved oval finishes from 0 to 12/20, so reach is the mechanism. Your ±0.04 m spread extends that reach to about e ≈ 0.06 m, the same drift at which race 2 lost the line, so it is the right test. The controller raises kp to 2.8 so that steering per metre stays close to race 2 despite the lower signal slope. Once race 3 reports, decide as follows. If s-bend and slalom line_loss falls below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06, keep ±0.04 m and 16 mm. If line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the spread is no longer the limiter, so hold the geometry. If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 with the new gain, move the sensors forward, as the 0.2 threshold requires.
requested_changes: Keep the ±0.04 m spread (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04) with 16 mm footprints and y = 0.05 for the next race, so this change is tested alone against the race 2 baseline.

If s-bend and slalom line_loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06 after race 3, hold the geometry and let the Integrator tune kp and base_speed. Do not try a narrower spread: race 2 already showed that narrowing removes the reach the line-loss evidence says is missing.
If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 after race 3, move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 to 0.065 with the spread and footprint unchanged, so the lead is the only geometry change in that race.
